documented_range.note: NO EVIDENCE ESTABLISHES THAT THIS PARTICULAR BUILDING EXISTED. It is the roof a reconstructed household requires - a meat market on the built streets, because a town of 3,265 does not walk three kilometres up the North Branch to Clybourne's for its dinner. The argument for the trade's presence in the town is in the household record and in the occupation census at data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json; the argument for THIS BUILDING is only that the household needs somewhere to be.

change_note: Raised by the inferred-household programme. A better-evidenced named building substitutes for this roof rather than standing beside it.

placement.position_note: INTERPRETIVE PLACEMENT ON A COMMITTED BLOCK FACE, NOT A RECOVERED LOT (T-0182). A meat market on the built streets, because a town of 3,265 does not walk three kilometres up the North Branch to Clybourne's for its dinner. This building does not stand where a centre in the programme put it: it stands on the north face of blk_lake_clark, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is set 0.80 m back from that lot line, which is the one line every record on this face stands on, and its bearing is the face's own rather than the zero a hand-authored centre carried. What the programme still chooses is where along the face it stands — 68.936 m from the face's west end, the position it already occupied, so this repair moves no building along the street. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, and that it was this trade's. The dataset's 20 m working georeference uncertainty applies on top of an already invented position, and standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot.
placement.symbolic_location: South Division, standing on the north frontage of blk_lake_clark, 68.9 m along that face

A shed is one plane over the whole 8.4 m of this plan where a gable climbs half of it, so across the 441 plans C1's own footprint band allows, 231 of them cannot reach the 15-20 ft ridge band the same family authors — at any eave in its 9-11 ft band and at any pitch between 22.6 and 36.9 degrees. This building's own plan is one of them.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5.5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

residents.why: inf_butcher_market is a structure record this parcel raises for the purpose, because no roof of the right family stood free in this district. The workplace is assigned from the reconstruction schedule's workshop and store families for this trade.
residents.basis: THIS BUILDING IS IN THE MODEL BECAUSE OF THIS HOUSEHOLD. Neither is documented: the household is inferred from the town's demonstrable needs and the roof was raised to house it. Its existence, position and size are all inventions, and the chips above say so.

persons.name: Willard Hale
persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. THE NAME IS INVENTED TOO, and `name_basis` beside it says so and says which pool it came from: this record used to carry a bare designation instead, on the reasoning that a surname would make it look like the documented layer, but a town of designations does not read as a town and the grade, this note and name_basis all say plainly which layer this is. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). THE FIRST OF 1 BUTCHER HOUSEHOLDS THIS LAYER RECONSTRUCTS. One butcher is documented: Clybourne, the government butcher, who is also a packer and lives three kilometres out on the North Branch. A town of 3,265 buys fresh meat daily and does not walk to the North Branch for it. One butchering household is inferred, keeping a market shop on the built streets.

residents.research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD - first of 1 butcher households in this layer, in the south division. One butcher is documented: Clybourne, the government butcher, who is also a packer and lives three kilometres out on the North Branch. A town of 3,265 buys fresh meat daily and does not walk to the North Branch for it. One butchering household is inferred, keeping a market shop on the built streets. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED BUILDING, RAISED FOR A RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). A meat market on the built streets, because a town of 3,265 does not walk three kilometres up the North Branch to Clybourne's for its dinner. It is NOT one of the anonymous count-units of the 665-roof programme: those are placed by aggregate mix and carry no occupant, while this one exists because the occupation census says the town held a household of this trade and no anonymous roof of the right family stood free in this district. It consumes one slot of its district's programme target rather than adding to it - see the accounting block in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json.
